extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX Coordinators, campus/school administrators, and institutional legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes the Department of Education's final-regulation standards for Title IX Coordinators and recipients: what coordinators must do when notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, how they must act (promptly/effectively), delegation and training expectations, and limits/guardrails on initiating complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator responsible for coordinating recipient compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's Title IX Coordinator is responsible for coordinating the recipient's compliance with its obligations under Title IX and the Department's implementing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Title IX Coordinator plays a central role and is responsible for coordinating comprehensive compliance, including oversight of responses to individual reports, addressing patterns/trends/risk factors, and ensuring the recipient provides an educational environment free from sex discrimination. The regulation text was revised to clarify that this role stems from the recipient's obligations and that the recipient remains ultimately responsible for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure recipient addresses conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(f) requires Title IX Coordinators to ensure a recipient addresses conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination through coordination of early interventions, equitable treatment, and provision of supportive measures and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is broader than responding only to sexual harassment; it covers any conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination. The Coordinator's oversight should include early intervention efforts, consistent treatment of complainants/respondents, and connecting individuals to supportive measures to end discrimination and prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient retains ultimate responsibility for Title IX compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient, not the Title IX Coordinator personally, is ultimately responsible for meeting all obligations under Title IX and the Department's regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory text clarifies the Coordinator 'coordinates the recipient's compliance' to emphasize institutional responsibility. The Department will hold the recipient accountable for meeting obligations even though the Coordinator has oversight duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator must treat complainants and respondents equitably, offer supportive measures, and provide grievance procedure information
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs (f)(1)(i)-(iii) require that a Title IX Coordinator treat complainants and respondents equitably, offer and coordinate supportive measures, and provide information about the recipient's grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These duties align with prior §106.44(a) obligations and qualify the nature of the Coordinator's response to ensure it is unbiased and supportive. The Coordinator may delegate certain responsibilities related to offering/coordinating supportive measures per §106.44(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and effective action to end, prevent recurrence, and remedy effects of sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator must take 'prompt' and 'effective' action to end sex discrimination, prevent its recurrence, and remedy its effects when notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No specific timeframe for 'prompt'; judged in context of the recipient's obligation to provide programs free from sex discrimination. 'Effective' means reasonable steps calibrated to address possible sex discrimination based on available information. If initial actions are not effective, the Coordinator must reevaluate and take additional steps. Failure to do so means the recipient fails to meet obligations. When sex discrimination is determined, the recipient must provide and implement remedies to restore or preserve equal access to programs/activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator duties apply when notified of conduct that 'reasonably may constitute' sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator requirements apply when the Coordinator is notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coordinator is not required to act on conduct that on its face could not constitute sex discrimination. §106.44(f)(2) permits the Coordinator to determine that alleged conduct could not constitute sex discrimination, in which case the (f)(1) duties do not apply. Coordinators should use their judgment and institutional perspective — including prior incidents — in making this assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to initiate complaints under limited, specific circumstances with guardrails
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators have longstanding authority to initiate complaints (i.e., sign a formal complaint) in limited circumstances and the final regulations preserve that authority with specified guardrails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinator-initiated complaints should balance complainant autonomy and recipient duty to address discrimination. Paragraphs (f)(v) and (vi) (and related discussion) include protections for complainant autonomy and safety to reduce risk of deterring reporting; initiation is discretionary and limited to circumstances described in the regulations and preamble. The Department considered comments on factors that coordinators should weigh when deciding to initiate complaints and retained mechanisms to prevent overbroad initiation against complainants' wishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinator may delegate specific duties and recipient may designate multiple coordinators
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may designate more than one employee to serve as a Title IX Coordinator and may delegate specific Title IX Coordinator duties to designees or allow a Coordinator to delegate duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation permits assigning duties to personnel best positioned to perform them, helps avoid conflicts of interest, and aligns with institutional administrative structure. Delegation is explicitly allowed by §106.8(a) and discussed for supportive measures in §106.44(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must ensure Title IX Coordinator effectiveness through authority, support, and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must give the Title IX Coordinator appropriate authority, support, and resources to ensure the Coordinator can effectively coordinate Title IX compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department rejects 'in name only' designations. Effectiveness depends on institutional support and the Coordinator's relationships and trust within the community. Recipients decide how to structure/support the role, including hiring full‑time Coordinators or providing staffing, as recommended by research and consistent with the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements on bias, impartiality, and scope of sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.8(d)(2)(iii) and (4) require recipients to train Title IX Coordinators on bias and impartiality; §106.8(d)(1) requires training for non-confidential employees on the scope of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training helps ensure Coordinators can identify when they may be biased or conflicted out of taking action and supports consistent assessments of whether conduct reasonably may constitute sex discrimination. The Department envisions Coordinators having unique expertise that informs their judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use institutional perspective and prior incidents in Coordinator assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator's assessment of whether conduct as alleged reasonably may constitute sex discrimination should draw on institutional expertise and awareness of prior conduct, incidents, or concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Coordinators coordinate compliance across reports and processes (supportive measures, grievance procedures, informal resolution), they may reasonably reach different conclusions than other employees about whether alleged conduct could constitute sex discrimination. This broader perspective justifies the Coordinator's discretion under §106.44(f)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding and managing conflicts of interest when Coordinator also performs underlying duties
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Title IX Coordinator both oversees compliance and performs underlying duties (e.g., coordinating supportive measures), recipients must address potential conflicts of interest by delegating resolution of efficacy concerns to an alternative individual when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.8(a)(2) permits delegation to other employees. If questions arise about the efficacy of actions taken by the Coordinator, the recipient should ensure an alternative individual resolves the concern to avoid bias. Training on bias and impartiality supports identification of conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may address conduct outside Title IX framework through other means
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations do not require Title IX Coordinator action for conduct that does not reasonably constitute sex discrimination and do not preclude recipients from addressing such conduct through other mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that coordinators and institutions retain flexibility to handle conduct that falls outside Title IX via other offices or processes, and the Department does not assert authority to require Title IX responses for conduct that could not constitute sex discrimination.
